record.original_question: For isotropic two-phase composites with complex effective permittivity, some known geometries place the effective permittivity on a particular bounding circular arc in the complex plane and can therefore attain maximal absorption in the quasistatic limit. Are there other microgeometries with isotropic effective permittivities whose effective responses also lie on that same arc?

evidence.quote: Problem 6: Are there other geometries with isotropic effective permittivities that lie on the arc?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider isotropic two-phase composite materials in the quasistatic limit, in which two isotropic homogeneous phases with complex (frequency-dependent) permittivities $\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2 \in \mathbb{C}$ are mixed in prescribed volume fractions $f_1, f_2 \ge 0$ with $f_1+f_2=1$. For any such microgeometry, the effective permittivity $\varepsilon_*$ is a complex scalar (because of isotropy) and is known to lie in a lens-shaped region of the complex plane whose boundary consists of two circular arcs determined by $\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2$ and the volume fractions; one of these arcs is the locus on which the effective absorption $\mathrm{Im}\,\varepsilon_*$ is maximized over isotropic mixtures of the two phases at the prescribed volume fraction. It is known that certain explicit microgeometries (for instance, doubly coated sphere/cylinder assemblages and certain hierarchical laminate constructions) produce isotropic effective permittivities lying exactly on this maximal-absorption bounding arc.

Question: Are there microgeometries, other than these known ones, whose effective permittivities are isotropic and also lie on this same maximal-absorption bounding arc? Equivalently, characterize all isotropic two-phase microstructures whose complex effective permittivity attains a point on this arc.
artifact.category_tag: Bounds on effective properties of composites
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Kern–Miller–Milton, 2020; Deshmukh–Milton, 2025) confirms that the maximal-absorption circular arc is optimal and is attained by doubly coated cylinder assemblages and certain rank-hierarchical laminates. However, no characterization is given of all isotropic microgeometries whose effective permittivities lie on this arc, and the question of whether other essentially different microgeometries achieve the same arc appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Tight Bounds on the Effective Complex Permittivity of Isotropic Composites and Related Problems
status_evidence.snippet: One of the circular arcs bounding the complex isotropic permittivity was improved and shown to be optimal, as it is attained by assemblages of doubly coated cylinders.
status_evidence.claim: The maximal-absorption arc is attained by doubly coated cylinder assemblages, but uniqueness of optimal microgeometries is not established.

status_evidence.title: Bounds on the Uniaxial Effective Complex Permittivity of Two-phase Composites and Optimal or Near Optimal Microstructures
status_evidence.snippet: Optimal rank-4 hierarchical laminate structures were identified that achieve all points on these conjectured bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Hierarchical laminates also realize points on optimal arcs, indicating multiple microstructure families can attain bounding arcs but no full characterization is given.
